Summarising Bayesian stochastic frontier models

Source: R/summary.sfmodel.R
summary.sfmodel.Rd

Summary method for class "sfmodel".

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
summary(object, ci = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.sfmodel'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object

an object of class "sfmodel_exp" or "sfmodel_hn", usually the result of a call to add_posterior_coefficients.

ci

a numeric between 0 and 1 specifying the probability of the credible band. Defaults to 0.95.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

x

an object of class "summary.sfmodel", usually the result of a call to summary.sfmodel.

digits

the number of significant digits to use when printing.

Value

summary.sfmodel returns a list of class "summary.sfmodel", which contains the following components:

coefficients

summary statistics of the posterior draws of the frontier coefficients and the two error components, ending in ESS, the effective sample size of each block. It is the number of independent draws the chain is worth, so the Monte Carlo error of a posterior mean is about its standard deviation divided by the square root of it. A value far below the number of draws is the sign that the chain needs to be longer, and in the four-component model it usually is.

efficiency

summary statistics of the posterior mean efficiency across units, or NULL if the inefficiency draws were not kept.

specifications

a list containing information on the model specification.

See also

efficiency for the unit-level scores.

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf(n = 200, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3), sigma_v = 0.2, par_u = 4)

model <- create_sfmodel_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d,
                            iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model <- add_posterior_coefficients(add_priors(model))

summary(model)
#> Bayesian stochastic frontier model
#> 
#> Call:
#> create_sfmodel_exp(formula = y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, iterations = 500, 
#>     burnin = 200)
#> 
#> Frontier:           production
#> Inefficiency:       exponential
#> Observations:       200
#> Units:              200
#> Draws:              500 after 200 burn-in, thinning 1
#> 
#> Posterior summary, 95% credible bands:
#>               mean     sd   2.5% median  97.5% ESS
#> (Intercept) 0.9820 0.0329 0.9185 0.9835 1.0460  20
#> x1          0.5048 0.0190 0.4688 0.5045 0.5431 146
#> x2          0.3045 0.0182 0.2666 0.3059 0.3361 178
#> sigma_v     0.1852 0.0243 0.1458 0.1830 0.2369  25
#> lambda      3.9853 0.5711 3.0847 3.9219 5.2840  21
#> 
#> Posterior mean efficiency, per observation:
#>   mean    min median    max 
#> 0.7969 0.2370 0.8400 0.9422
